templates.name: PR Review
templates.body:
Review the PR at ${URL}. Use the PR skill. First decide which focus areas apply to the PR - for each focus area that you skip, it must be justified. A reviewer should review 4-7 focus areas. For a tiny/simple PR, two reviewer subagents can handle all focus areas. Each reviewer must be a different subagent, and needs to be assigned a reviewer persona - just point the subagent to the persona to load as its identity before reviewing. Make sure to map reviewers to matching focus areas. Feedback from each reviewer must be validated by a different reviewer with a different persona. Multiple reviewers with the same persona can be created. Approve the PR unless there is a good reason not to. Comment only if you don't think it should be approved, be clear why.

IMPORTANT: you should limit how many rounds of actual review you do. There should be a maximum of 2 rounds of new feedback; if you are on the third round of review, just make sure that all previous feedback has either been fixed, or has a reasonable justification for not fixing (like deferring to a future PR instead of this one, or that it's just internal/test code). If you are on round 3 or higher, do not do a normal review, just verify that previous feedback has either been fixed or a non-fix has been justified.

ALSO IMPORTANT: Do not withhold approval due to merge conflicts or failing CI. Those have to be resolved anyway to merge.

templates.name: Subagent guidance
templates.body:
Important: Subagent Guidance

Use subagents for your work. These should be general purpose subagents, not "explore" subagents. When doing research or implementing, plan out your work in a way so that you can break it up into manageable steps, and then delegate each of those steps to a subagent. This keeps your context from bloating and is very important to reduce costs and compactions. It also keeps you responsive to any coordination while the tasks are running in the background. 

Also consider the next steps towards your goal, and think about if you can parallelize any of them. If so, and if you are not currently running many things in parallel already, do so. It will speed up completion of the goal.

Do not abuse the inline tool allowance, or it will be disabled.

templates.name: Set Goal
templates.body: Set a goal for the requirements I gave you, and make sure it spells out the success criteria clearly and in enough detail that it will be easy to know when you're done.

templates.name: Worker Anxiety
templates.body:
Create a recurring 30-minute reminder on your own worker window, not on the supervisor window. Don't delete any existing reminders, just add this new one. Before setting it, write the reminder body so its FIRST sentence is exactly:

LAUNCH A READ-ONLY LUNA SUBAGENT NOW.

The subagent must inspect your tmux window, recent commits, current diff, and test results, then say whether you are on track for ${project_goal}. It must flag unnecessary robot-review/fix loops, unrelated work, scope drift, a different approach than ${project_goal} requires, lack of progress toward the remaining deliverables, stale or unverified claims, or anything that could disrupt a live or shared system.

After that opening instruction, summarize the project/goal and its exact requirements and current explicit product decisions: ${project_goal}. The audit should use those requirements to judge whether the work is on track, not substitute a different goal.

The reminder must be motivating and practical, not generic. It should name the next concrete step, the remaining deliverable, or the blocker owner. After creating it, immediately list the reminder and show its exact body (or at least the first sentence and requirements) so I can verify that the subagent instruction is visibly first. Do not just say it was created.

templates.name: Supervisor Anxiety
templates.body:
Create a recurring 30-minute reminder on the supervisor window, not on any worker window. Don't delete any existing reminders, just add this new one. Target the active long-running priority and the workers coordinating on it, rather than a single task. The priority is: ${project_goal}.

Before setting it, write the reminder body so its FIRST sentence is exactly:

LAUNCH A READ-ONLY LUNA SUBAGENT NOW.

The subagent must inspect the supervisor tmux window, the active priority record, every assigned worker’s window and state, recent mailbox handoffs, commits, current diffs, and test results. It must say whether the priority’s orchestration is on track for ${project_goal}. It must flag unnecessary robot-review/fix loops, idle or misassigned workers, duplicated or conflicting work, unrelated work, scope drift, a different approach than ${project_goal} requires, missing handoffs or dependencies, lack of progress toward the remaining deliverables, stale or unverified claims, or anything that could disrupt a live or shared system.

After that opening instruction, summarize the project/goal and its exact requirements and current explicit product decisions: ${project_goal}. The audit should keep every worker aligned to that priority and should not invent adjacent scope.

After the audit, take one concrete supervisor action if needed: send the right worker a focused next step, resolve a dependency, stop a needless loop, or identify the owner and next verification point for a blocker. Do not modify code, disturb a live or shared system, or claim progress without evidence. Keep the reminder practical and motivating: protect the priority, keep workers moving, and name what should happen before the next 30-minute check.

After creating it, immediately list the reminder and show its exact body so I can verify that the subagent instruction is visibly first. Do not just say it was created.

templates.name: Scope Creep Check
templates.body: Have a subagent double-check that all of the changes in this PR are in support of the ticket, and that no additional scope has crept in.

templates.name: Consistency Check
templates.body: Have a subagent go through an audit to see if we are using existing patterns for this PR. Check each individual file in the PR to make sure that it uses existing patterns and doesn't invent any new ones - there should be at least one or two places in the codebase that use the same pattern. The key priority here is consistency with the existing codebase, it outweighs "doing it better".

templates.name: Address Feedback
templates.body:
Take a look at open threads on this PR. Address any feedback that should be addressed, then get the changes pushed up. Once changes are pushed up, reply to each thread and resolve them if the feedback was addressed.

Also remember that ideally we would have caught any issues already. Make sure to improve robot review heuristics and capture any domain knowledge in the KB. If there are any best practices that can be learned from this, also capture in the KB. Make sure any new heuristics aren't too narrow, they should be generally applicable. DO NOT RUN robot review, just update heuristics based on the PR feedback.

Set a goal to get this done, and make sure it spells out the success criteria clearly and in enough detail that it will be easy to know when you're done.

templates.name: New Ticket
templates.body: Get a worker started on ${ticket}. Make sure that the worker name is both descriptive and begins with the ticket number (the same thing as the tmux window name), and inform the worker by mailbox what their window name is. Create a new worktree, then start a new window in that worktree and hand off the task to the worker. Make sure to include instructions for the worker to set a goal with clear success criteria. Also get the ticket marked as in progress (if applicable). Make sure the worker loads the worker skill.

templates.name: Green CI
templates.body: Check your PR for CI failures or merge conflicts. If any are found, set a goal to get these fixed. You need to get your PR free of merge conflicts and CI failures, CI must be green. Also set a 15 minute recurring reminder to keep checking it. You can remove the reminder and goal once it's green. Inform me once it is.

templates.name: Supervisor Status Update
templates.body: Tell me at a high level so it's really easy to understand what everybody's status is right now. Is anyone blocked or has anyone come to a halt when they should be moving?

templates.name: PR Sweep
templates.body:
Sweep only the configured org for open PRs (see ~/AGENTS.md) that need review. These should be PRs not authored by Wolfgang. Either Wolfgang has already reviewed them and they have new changes since, Wolfgang has been explicitly requested or re-requested. Those are the PRs to include in the sweep. For each PR, in sequence, do the following:

Use the PR skill. First decide which focus areas apply to the PR - for each focus area that you skip, it must be justified. A reviewer should review 4-7 focus areas. For a tiny/simple PR, two reviewer subagents can handle all focus areas. Each reviewer must be a different subagent, and needs to be assigned a reviewer persona - just point the subagent to the persona to load as its identity before reviewing. Make sure to map reviewers to matching focus areas. Feedback from each reviewer must be validated by a different reviewer with a different persona. Multiple reviewers with the same persona can be created. Approve the PR unless there is a good reason not to. Comment only if you don't think it should be approved, be clear why.

IMPORTANT: you should limit how many rounds of actual review you do. There should be a maximum of 2 rounds of new feedback; if you are on the third round of review, just make sure that all previous feedback has either been fixed, or has a reasonable justification for not fixing (like deferring to a future PR instead of this one, or that it's just internal/test code). If you are on round 3 or higher, do not do a normal review, just verify that previous feedback has either been fixed or a non-fix has been justified.

ALSO IMPORTANT: Do not withhold approval due to merge conflicts or failing CI. Those have to be resolved anyway to merge.

templates.name: Unblock Yourself
templates.body: Remember that you are authorized to make any and all decisions to become unblocked. If you discover any decisions that need to be made, use the wolfgang persona to make the best decision. You are authorized to install, change, push, or otherwise make mutations to proceed towards completion of the RPC project. Do not allow yourself to become blocked. To be clear: DO NOT WAIT ON THE USER FOR ANYTHING. you already have everything you need to get all the way to completion. Once you complete a phase, start the next phase until this project is fully completed.

templates.name: Parallelize
templates.body: Consider the next steps towards your goal, and think about if you can parallelize any of them. If so, and if you are not currently running many things in parallel already, do so. It will speed up completion of the goal.

templates.name: Supervisor Sweep
templates.body:
Run this in a subagent:

Enumerate the list of all workers. For each worker, if they have an open PR, check it for the following: CI failures, merge conflicts, unaddressed feedback. If the PR has any of these, get the worker to set a goal to work on it. CI must be green and free of merge conflicts, and all new feedback must either be addressed (strongly preferred) or replied to if there is a good reason not to address it. All threads should be replied to, addressed feedback threads should be resolved.
